title: COP31 climate summit negotiators work into overtime to finalize draft agreement
seoTitle: COP31 climate summit negotiators work into overtime
dek: Negotiators at the COP31 summit in Antalya are working through a second day of overtime to reach a consensus on a final climate agreement. The latest draft omits explicit mentions of fossil fuels, sparking debate among participating nations.
happened: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, entered a second day of overtime on 22 November as negotiators attempted to finalize a global climate agreement. According to COP31 President Murat Kurum, a new draft text was presented to delegations early on 22 November following intensive consultations between Australia, Turkey, and nearly 200 nations. The summit, which was originally scheduled to conclude on 21 November, faced delays due to disagreements over the inclusion of fossil fuels in the final text. While an initial draft on 18 November called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, a subsequent version released on 20 November removed these references following objections from Saudi Arabia and other oil-producing nations. The current draft acknowledges a previous commitment to transition away from fossil fuels and recognizes that global warming is on track to exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius threshold. Delegations were given until 06:00 GMT on 22 November to review the text before a scheduled plenary session to approve the deal. If consensus is not reached, the negotiations could be suspended until next year.

sides.says: COP31 President Murat Kurum stated, "We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon." He added, "We are closer than ever to agreement on the remaining issues."
EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra stated that if the bloc could not secure necessary climate action, "then there's no deal," adding that "it's better to have no deal than to have a bad deal."
According to observers, Saudi Arabia and other major oil-producing nations pushed for the removal of explicit fossil fuel phase-out language from the draft text.
In a letter to the co-hosts, 100 groups warned the summit was "on course to preside over one of the most disappointing COPs" and urged leaders to save the negotiations from becoming a "low point."

next: Delegations were expected to reconvene at 06:00 GMT on 22 November to decide whether to approve the latest draft agreement.
summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, has extended into a second day of overtime as negotiators struggle to reach a consensus on a final agreement. The latest draft text, released on 22 November, omits explicit references to phasing out fossil fuels, a move that has drawn criticism from various delegations and civil society groups. The summit, co-hosted by Turkey and Australia, aims to address global warming and climate finance. If a consensus is not reached by the participating nations, the negotiations risk being suspended until next year, a rare occurrence in the history of UN climate summits.
